blurb: Massive Italian guardian known for loose skin and heavy facial wrinkles
description: The Neapolitan Mastiff is a massive Italian guard dog from Southern Italy, with loose, heavily wrinkled skin and a short coat, usually black, grey or leaden.
answer: The Neapolitan Mastiff, or Mastino Napoletano, is a large, massive mastiff-type breed from Southern Italy, descended from the region's traditional guard dogs. It stands about 60 to 75 cm tall, weighs roughly 50 to 70 kg, and is known for its abundant loose skin.

body: The breed derives from the traditional catch and guard dogs of Southern Italy and is closely related to the Cane Corso. Piero Scanziani began selecting the breed in 1947 after seeing one at an exhibition in Naples in 1946. He drew up the first standard, which the Ente Nazionale della Cinofilia Italiana recognised in 1949, and the FCI fully accepted the breed in 1956.

The Neapolitan Mastiff is large, massive and powerful, with a body about 15% longer than it is tall. Its skin is abundant and loose, hanging in heavy wrinkles on the head. Preferred colours are black, grey and leaden; mahogany, fawn, fulvous, hazelnut, dove-grey and isabelline are also accepted. Any coat may be brindled, and small white markings on the chest and toes are tolerated.

The source text gives little detail on temperament. Given its background as a guard dog, the breed is generally described in guardian terms; the breed standard and breed clubs give a fuller account of its expected character.

Sources give little specific guidance on care or exercise. As with other very large, heavy breeds, owners generally need enough space and consistent handling, and the skin folds are a point to keep an eye on during routine grooming.

The breed is relatively short-lived: dogs may be expected to live up to about 10 years, and its reported median lifespan of 9.3 years is well below the 12.5-year median for all dogs. The source text does not name specific conditions; breed clubs generally recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: How long do Neapolitan Mastiffs live?
faq.a: They may be expected to live up to about 10 years, with a reported median lifespan of 9.3 years, lower than the median for dogs overall.

faq.q: How big does a Neapolitan Mastiff get?
faq.a: It typically stands about 60 to 75 cm at the withers and weighs about 50 to 70 kg.

faq.q: Is the Neapolitan Mastiff recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI accepted it in 1956 and lists it as breed number 197 in Group 2, with Italy as the country of origin.
